question: If a sum of ₹8,20,000 is invested for a year at 6% per annum compounded half yearly, then find the compound interest.
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

For **half-yearly compounding**, the rate becomes 3% (6 ÷ 2) and the time periods become 2 (1 year × 2).

Effective rate for 2 periods of 3% each = 3 + 3 + (3 × 3)/100 = **6.09%**.

Compound Interest = 6.09% of ₹8,20,000

⇒ CI = 8,20,000 × (6.09 ÷ 100) = 8,200 × 6.09 = ₹49,938.

**∴ The correct answer is ₹49,938.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Principal (P) = **₹8,20,000**, Rate (R) = **6% p.a.**, Time (T) = **1 year**.

Since the interest is **compounded half-yearly**:

⇒ New Rate (r) = 6% ÷ 2 = **3% per half-year**.

⇒ Number of periods (n) = 1 × 2 = **2 half-years**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/d9fe6840fca3933ff8126522d2744815382611da06fe40fe63d18eea2f22de7b.png] 

**Formula:** Amount (A) = P(1 + r/100)ⁿ

⇒ A = 8,20,000 × (1 + 3/100)²

⇒ A = 8,20,000 × (103/100) × (103/100)

⇒ A = 8,20,000 × 1.03 × 1.03

⇒ A = 8,20,000 × 1.0609 = **₹8,69,938**

⇒ Compound Interest (CI) = Amount − Principal

⇒ CI = 8,69,938 − 8,20,000

⇒ CI = ₹49,938

**∴ The correct answer is ₹49,938.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Compounding Half-Yearly Rule

When interest is compounded half-yearly, the annual rate is divided by 2 (R/2) and the time period is multiplied by 2 (2T).

Successive Percentage Formula

For two successive interest rates x% and y%, the effective interest rate is (x + y + xy/100)%.

Compounding Quarterly Rule

When interest is compounded quarterly, the annual rate is divided by 4 (R/4) and the time period is multiplied by 4 (4T).
